64226-ecclesiastical-history-of-england-.title: Death Of Oliver Cromwell.
64226-ecclesiastical-history-of-england-.creator: John Stoughton.
64226-ecclesiastical-history-of-england-.description: A book by John Stoughton.. All ecclesiastical power in England having been long before snatched from royal hands, the death of Charles I. produced no effect upon the condition of the Church. The control of its political destinies had from the year 1641 rested with the House of Commons; and with the remnant of that assembly the control continued, when the kingdom became a Commonwealth in name as well as in fact.

68195-a-happy-half-century-and-other-ess.title: _And Other Essays_
68195-a-happy-half-century-and-other-ess.creator: Agnes Repplier, Litt. D.
68195-a-happy-half-century-and-other-ess.description: A book by Agnes Repplier, Litt. D.. ntury and the first twenty-five years of the nineteenth make up my chosen period, and that my motive for so choosing is contemptible. It was not a time distinguished--in England at least--for wit or wisdom, for public virtues or for private charm; but it _was_ a time when literary reputations were so cheaply gained that nobody needed to despair of one.

arxiv-2101-08533.title: Eliminate Deviation with Deviation for Data Augmentation and a General Multi-modal Data Learning Method
arxiv-2101-08533.creator: Yunpeng Gong, Liqing Huang, Lifei Chen, {lqhuang, clfei}@fjnu.edu.cn
arxiv-2101-08533.description: Abstract One of the challenges of computer vision is that it needs to adapt to color deviations in changeable environments. Therefore, minimizing the adverse effects of color deviation on the prediction is one of the main goals of vision task. Current solutions focus on using generative models to augment training data to enhance the invariance of input variation.

arxiv-2402-02788.title: Artificial-intelligence-based surrogate solution of dissipative quantum dynamics: physics-informed reconstruction of the universal propagator
arxiv-2402-02788.creator: Jiaji Zhang, Carlos L. Benavides-Riveros, Lipeng Chen
arxiv-2402-02788.description: Abstract The accurate (or even approximate) solution of the equations that govern the dynamics of dissipative quantum systems remains a challenging task for quantum science. While several algorithms have been designed to solve those equations with different degrees of flexibility, they rely mainly on highly expensive iterative schemes.

arxiv-2409-12166.title: Synchrotron self-Compton in a radiative-adiabatic fireball scenario: Modelling the multiwavelength observations in some Fermi /LAT bursts 2015 Synchrotron self-Compton in a radiative-adiabatic fireball scenario: Modelling the multiwavelength observations in some Fermi /LAT bursts – 7
arxiv-2409-12166.creator: Nissim Fraija, P. Veres, B. Betancourt Kamenetskaia A. Galvan-Gamez M.G. Dainotti Simone Dichiara, R. L. Becerra
arxiv-2409-12166.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nissim Fraija, P. Veres, B. Betancourt Kamenetskaia A. Galvan-Gamez M.G. Dainotti Simone Dichiara, R. L. Becerra. Energetic GeV photons expected from the closest and the most energetic Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) provide an unique opportunity to study the very-high-energy emission as well as the possible correlations with lower energy bands in realistic GRB afterglow models. In the standard GRB afterglow model, the relativistic homogeneous shock is usually considered to be fully adiabatic, however, it could be partially radiative.

arxiv-2411-17636.title: MALMM: Multi-Agent Large Language Models for Zero-Shot Robotics Manipulation
arxiv-2411-17636.creator: Harsh Singh, Rocktim Jyoti Das, Mingfei Han, Preslav Nakov, Ivan Laptev
arxiv-2411-17636.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable planning abilities across various domains, including robotics manipulation and navigation. While recent efforts in robotics have leveraged LLMs both for high-level and low-level planning, these approaches often face significant challenges, such as hallucinations in long-horizon tasks and limited adaptability due to the generation of plans in a single pass without real-time feedback.

arxiv-2502-00101.title: Characterization of the Teledyne COSMOS Camera: A Large Format CMOS Image Sensor for Astronomy
arxiv-2502-00101.creator: Christopher Layden, Jill Juneau, Gustav Pettersson, Nathan Lourie, Benjamin Schneider, Beverly LaMarr, F. Elio Angile, Fadi Farag, Michelle Luo, Zhi Zheng Ong, Gabor Furesz
arxiv-2502-00101.description: Abstract The Teledyne COSMOS-66 is a next-generation CMOS camera designed for astronomical imaging, featuring a large-format sensor ( 8120 × 8120 8120\times 8120 pixels, each 10 ​ μ ​ m 10\,\mu m wide), high quantum efficiency, high frame rates and a correlated multi-sampling mode that achieves low read noise.

arxiv-2505-08348.title: Geometry of Semantics in Next-Token Prediction: How Optimization Implicitly Organizes Linguistic Representations
arxiv-2505-08348.creator: Yize Zhao, Christos Thrampoulidis
arxiv-2505-08348.description: Abstract We investigate how next-token prediction (NTP) optimization leads language models to extract and organize semantic structure from text. Our analysis, based on a tractable mathematical model and controlled synthetic data, reveals that NTP implicitly guides models to factor a centered support matrix encoding context-to-next-token co-occurrence patterns via singular value decomposition (SVD).

arxiv-2506-20837.title: A Black Hole is Born: 3D GRMHD Simulation of Black Hole Formation from Core-Collapse
arxiv-2506-20837.creator: Goni Halevi, Swapnil Shankar, Philipp Mösta, Roland Haas, Erik Schnetter
arxiv-2506-20837.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Goni Halevi, Swapnil Shankar, Philipp Mösta, Roland Haas, Erik Schnetter. We present the first three-dimensional, fully general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (3D GRMHD) simulation of a black hole (BH) formed from the collapsed core of a massive star. The ability to self-consistently capture the birth of a compact remnant in 3D is crucial for modeling natal BH properties (including masses, spins, and kicks), which are of particular interest in the era of gravitational wave astronomy.

pmc-10719394.title: Effect of ocean outfall discharge volume and dissolved inorganic nitrogen load on urban eutrophication outcomes in the Southern California Bight
pmc-10719394.creator: Minna Ho, Fayçal Kessouri, Christina A. Frieder, Martha Sutula, Daniele Bianchi, James C. McWilliams
pmc-10719394.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Climate change is increasing drought severity worldwide. Ocean discharges of municipal wastewater are a target for potable water recycling. Potable water recycling would reduce wastewater volume; however, the effect on mass nitrogen loading is dependent on treatment. In cases where nitrogen mass loading is not altered or altered minimally, this practice has the potential to influence spatial patterns in coastal eutrophication.

pmc-11486905.title: OTUD5 promotes end-joining of deprotected telomeres by promoting ATM-dependent phosphorylation of KAP1S824
pmc-11486905.creator: Shiu Yeung Lam, Ruben van der Lugt, Aurora Cerutti, Zeliha Yalçin, Alexander M. Thouin, Marco Simonetta, Jacqueline J. L. Jacobs
pmc-11486905.description: Appropriate repair of damaged DNA and the suppression of DNA damage responses at telomeres are essential to preserve genome stability. DNA damage response (DDR) signaling consists of cascades of kinase-driven phosphorylation events, fine-tuned by proteolytic and regulatory ubiquitination. It is not fully understood how crosstalk between these two major classes of post-translational modifications impact DNA repair at deprotected telomeres.

pmc-11624745.title: Elucidating the role of physical exercises in alleviating stroke-associated homeostatic dysregulation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11624745.creator: Vanina Myuriel Villagra Moran, Irin Sultana Nila, Rajesh Madhuvilakku, Dewan Md Sumsuzzman, Zeeshan Ahmad Khan, Yonggeun Hong
pmc-11624745.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThis study aimed to investigate the role of physical exercises as a non-pharmacological intervention for ameliorating post-stroke dysregulated homeostatic parameters.MethodsEmbase, PubMed, PEDro, ISI Web of Science and CENTRAL were searched until April 2024. Parallel randomised controlled trials (RCTs) analysing the effect of post-stroke physical exercises (PSPE) on homeostatic parameters such as blood glucose, oxygen consumption (VO2), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), systolic (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) in individuals with stroke were selected.ResultsSixteen RCTs (n=698) were included.

pmc-13329062.creator: Gerda Prakopimaite, Magdalena Pfaff, Eddy J Davelaar, Lisa Quadt, Malgorzata Raczek, Naji Tabet, Alan J Gow, Carol Holland, Dorina Cadar, Tonya J Roberts
pmc-13329062.description: Background and ObjectivesAs populations age, extending healthy life expectancy and reducing morbidity are priorities. Cognitive frailty, the co-occurrence of cognitive impairment and physical frailty without dementia, may offer a window for prevention. However, there is limited evidence on how cognitive frailty is understood, which may undermine recognition and risk reduction.
